children.name: DocumentGroup(newDocument:editor:)
children.summary: The editable form: the value you pass is the template for every file created via New, and the closure gets a configuration carrying a binding to the live document.

children.name: DocumentGroup(viewing:viewer:)
children.summary: A read-only counterpart that registers the app as a viewer for a document type without offering New, Save, or editing.

children.name: DocumentGroup(editing:contentType:editor:prepareDocument:)
children.summary: Backs each document with its own SwiftData store for the given model type; prepareDocument seeds the container before a new file is shown (iOS 17, macOS 14).

children.name: FileDocumentConfiguration
children.summary: What the editor and viewer closures receive: the document (with a binding projection), its file URL once saved, and whether edits are allowed.

discussion: DocumentGroup binds a FileDocument or ReferenceFileDocument type to editor windows, inheriting the platform's new/open/save/rename machinery, recents, and iCloud integration.
name: DocumentGroup
summary: Document-based app scenes with open/save for free.

children.name: DocumentGroupLaunchScene(_:actions:background:)
children.summary: The common shape: a title, a row of action buttons for creating or importing documents, and a full-bleed view drawn behind everything.

children.name: DocumentGroupLaunchScene(_:actions:background:overlayAccessoryView:)
children.summary: Layers a decorative view above the title card, positioned using the frames the geometry proxy reports.

children.name: DocumentLaunchGeometryProxy
children.summary: The proxy handed to accessory closures, exposing the scene's frame and the title view's frame so decorations can anchor to either.

children.name: NewDocumentButton
children.summary: The stock launch-scene action that creates a blank document and opens it; give it a custom title or rely on the default label.

discussion: Added at WWDC '24, DocumentGroupLaunchScene gives document apps the title-screen treatment — hero background, title, and action buttons for creating or opening documents — replacing the bare document browser as the first screen.
name: DocumentGroupLaunchScene
summary: A designed launch experience for document-based iOS apps.

children.name: MenuBarExtra(_:systemImage:content:)
children.summary: Shows an SF Symbol in the status bar with the title used for accessibility; the content builder becomes the pull-down menu.

children.name: MenuBarExtra(_:isInserted:content:)
children.summary: Ties the status item's presence to a Boolean binding, so a preference toggle can add or remove it while the app runs.

children.name: MenuBarExtra(content:label:)
children.summary: Supplies an arbitrary view as the status-item label, which is how you show live text or a symbol that changes with state.

children.name: .menuBarExtraStyle(_:)
children.summary: Picks between the default pull-down menu (.menu) and a floating panel (.window) that can host any SwiftUI hierarchy.

discussion: MenuBarExtra installs a status item with either a pull-down menu or, with the window style, a full SwiftUI popover panel. Apps can be menu-bar-only by making it their sole scene. This very app uses one for quick topic search.
name: MenuBarExtra
summary: Puts your app in the macOS menu bar.

discussion: Declaring a Settings scene gives the app the standard Settings menu item, ⌘, shortcut, and window. TabViews inside render as settings panes.
name: Settings
summary: The macOS Settings window, wired to the app menu.

children.name: Window(_:id:content:)
children.summary: The sole initializer: a title for the Windows menu and a required id that openWindow uses to bring the single instance forward.

children.name: .windowResizability(_:)
children.summary: Derives the window's resize limits from its content (.contentSize or .contentMinSize) instead of letting the user drag it anywhere.

children.name: .defaultPosition(_:)
children.summary: Chooses where the window lands the first time it opens, as a UnitPoint on the screen; the user's later placement is restored after that.

children.name: .windowLevel(_:)
children.summary: Moves the window to a different layer — .floating keeps a palette above ordinary windows, .desktop pins it beneath them (macOS 15).

discussion: Where WindowGroup multiplies, Window guarantees exactly one instance — right for dashboards, about panels, and utility windows. It joins the Windows menu automatically and opens via its id.
name: Window
summary: A single, unique window on macOS.

children.name: WindowGroup(_:content:)
children.summary: The basic form: a titled group of identical windows.

children.name: WindowGroup(id:content:)
children.summary: Adds a stable identifier so openWindow can target the group.

children.discussion: The system opens one window per distinct value and hands the content closure a binding to an optional — it is nil when a window opens without a presented value, as from the New Window menu command, so the content must handle that case. openWindow(value:) reuses an existing window when the value already has one, and the defaultValue: overload supplies a fallback that makes the binding non-optional.
children.name: WindowGroup(for:content:)
children.summary: Presents a window per value — one editor per document id.

discussion: WindowGroup can instantiate any number of identical windows (macOS and iPadOS) from one declaration. Give it an id or a presented value type to open specific windows programmatically through the openWindow environment action.
name: WindowGroup
summary: The standard scene for an app's main windows.
